ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AB \parallel CD$, and the line $MN$ intersects $AB$ and $CD$ at points $E$ and $F$, respectively, with $\angle NEB = 58^\circ$. If $EG \perp AB$, and $EH$ bisects $\angle NEG$ and intersects $CD$ at point $H$, what is the measure of $\angle BEH$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $EG\perp AB$, it follows that $\angle BEG=90^\circ$, \\
hence, $\angle BEH=90^\circ-\angle GEH$, \\
since $EH$ bisects $\angle NEG$, \\
it follows that $\angle GEH= \frac{1}{2}\angle NEG=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-\angle MEG)$, \\
from (1) we know $\angle AEM=58^\circ$, and since $EG\perp AB$, \\
thus, $\angle MEG=90^\circ-\angle AEM=90^\circ-58^\circ=32^\circ$, \\
hence, $\angle GEH=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-32^\circ)=74^\circ$, \\
thus, $\angle BEH=90^\circ-74^\circ=\boxed{16^\circ}$.

From E, draw EG upward, and EG is perpendicular to AB; from E, draw EH toward the upper right, intersecting the upper straight line CD at H. Reasoning: It is known that ∠NEB = 58°. Because EN and EM are opposite rays, and EB and EA are opposite rays, ∠AEM and ∠NEB are vertical angles, therefore ∠AEM = 58°. Also because EG ⟂ AB, ∠AEG = ∠BEG = 90°. In the right angle ∠AEG, ∠MEG = 90° - ∠AEM = 90° - 58° = 32°. Since EN and EM are opposite rays, ∠NEG = 180° - ∠MEG = 180° - 32° = 148°. EH bisects ∠NEG, therefore ∠GEH = 148° ÷ 2 = 74°. Finally, ∠BEH = ∠BEG - ∠GEH = 90° - 74° = 16°.
